Firefox doesn't have a feature that starts it with an empty, completely reset profile, but it does have a built‐in profile manager. firefox -ProfileManager starts it with the profile manager to let you choose a profile or create a new one. firefox -P <profile-name> lets you skip the manager and start with the profile you named. This is a Python script for selecting a random file on one or more directories. It's pretty useful when you have a big movie/series/comic collection and you want to pick a episode/movie/issue to watch/read without having to think a lot about it. Some examples:

randompicker "The Simpsons" #selects a random The Simpsons episode
randompicker "Action movies" "Hero movies" #if both are folders will select a random action or drama movie (includes subfolders)
randompicker . #selects a file from the current directory and subdirectories

Depending on how you're using it you may want to add/remove extensions from FORBIDDEN.

Source:

#!/usr/bin/python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import os,sys,random

if len(sys.argv)==1:
 raise Exception('Usage: randompicker [dir1] [dir2] [...]')

TEMP='/tmp/randompicker'
FORBIDDEN=['.srt','.sub','.jpg','.directory','.sfv','.idx','.nfo','.html','.txt','.ini']

dirs=''
for dir in sys.argv[1:]:
 dirs+='"'+dir+'" '
os.system('find {} -type f > {}'.format(dirs,TEMP))
files=open('/tmp/randompicker').readlines()
pick=False
while pick==False:
 pick=files[random.randint(0,len(files))][:-1]
 lowerpick=pick.lower()
 for f in FORBIDDEN:
 if lowerpick.endswith(f):
 pick=False
 break
print(pick)

#!/usr/bin/python

from Tkinter import * #import all the parts of Tkinter so they can be used
import sys
import os

#this script produces an on-screen alert box with text $P1. 
#if parameters $P2 and $P3 are defined, a second button labeled with $P2 will be
# shown and it will send os terminal command $P3

class Alert(Frame):

 def __init__(self, master=None, message="Error: No Message", action=None):
 
 self.message = message;
 self.action = action;

 # initiate a frame 
 Frame.__init__(self, master)
 self.pack()
 
 # initiage the message panel
 self.messagePanel = Label(self, text=message)
 self.messagePanel.pack({"side":"top"})

 # initiate the "OK" button
 self.OK = Button(self) #initialize a button
 self.OK["text"] = "OK" #set the text on the button
 self.OK["fg"] = "black" #set the text color of the button
 self.OK["command"] = self.quit #set the command tied to the button
 self.OK.pack({"fill":"x"})
 
 # if it exists, add a command button
 if not(action is None):
 self.commandButton = Button(self)
 self.commandButton["text"]=action["label"]
 self.commandButton["command"]=self.genericFunction
 self.commandButton.pack({"fill": "x"})

 def genericFunction(self):
 os.system(self.action["command"])
 

# if the alert script is called from the command line, make and run the alert 
# with command line arguments
if __name__ == "__main__":
 # initiate a Tk instance
 root = Tk()

 # Parse inputs
 # input case: message only
 if len(sys.argv)==2:
 message = sys.argv[1]
 # initiate an instance of the Alert class called popup
 popup = Alert(master=root, message=message)
 # input case: message and command
 elif len(sys.argv)==4:
 message = sys.argv[1]
 action = dict(label=sys.argv[2], command=sys.argv[3])
 # initiate an instance of the Alert class called popup
 popup = Alert(master=root, message=message, action=action)
 else:
 message = "invoke with 1 or 3 parameters. $P1=message, $P2=action label, $P3=terminal command"
 popup = Alert(master=root, message=message)
 
 # run the Tk mainloop function that popup inherited from Frame
 popup.mainloop()
 # clean up
 root.destroy()

rsync-safety.bash

#!/bin/bash

#specify source and destination folders
sourceFolder=/home/SamLJackson/mainHomeFolder
destinFolder=/mnt/sdb/backups

#make sure the source directory exists
if [ ! -d "$sourceFolder" ]; then
 echo "$sourceFolder does not exist, exiting..."
 exit
fi

#make sure the destination directory exists
if [ ! -d "$destinFolder" ]; then
 echo "$destinFolder does not exist, exiting..."
 exit
fi

#create the log file
datestamp=$(date +%Y-%m-%d-%H-%M-%S)
fname="./backup$datestamp.log"
touch $fname
echo "sync event initiated on $(date +%B) $(date +%d) of $(date +%Y) at $(date +
%H:%M:%S)">$fname
echo "source:$sourceFolder">>$fname
echo "destin:$destinFolder">>$fname
echo "">>$fname

# sync folder A to backup image
# -a archival mode, preserve timestamps and permissions, work recursively 
# through folders, etc.
# -v verbose mode, produce a record of some kind
# --delete if a file doesn't exist in the source, delete it from the backu
# p
# $sourceFolder is the active file structure
# $destinFolder is where the files are backed up to
# 2>&1 dumps the stderr and stdout streams
# | tee pipes all the stderr and stdout streams through the tee command wh
# ich simultaneously
# prints to the screen and to a file (so I can watch as a log is m
# ade)
# >>$fname records the output into the log file
rsync -av --delete $sourceFolder $destinFolder 2>&1 | tee $fname

Japanese factory workers also famously had more input into operations than their Western peers (although the relationship between floor workers and management was more complicated than you think; the workers had an obligation to come up with improvements).

The best example of a socialist system is in the book The Dispossesed, by Ursula LeGuin. Trust me, if you have not read it yet, you need to. It’s beautifully written, with a very spare style, as well as thought-provoking."
